\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputWindow}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Copying an input window to a work tape]
\lean{Turing.exists_inputWindowCopyTM}
\label{Turing.exists_inputWindowCopyTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
For every natural number $k$ and distinct work-tape indices $j,d$, there exist a finite
state set, a deterministic $k$-work-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, entry
and completion states, and a constant $C$. Given a configuration on input $z$ in the
entry state with input head at position $p+1$ and tape $j$ storing a word $w$, let $y$
be the initial segment of $z$ starting at position $p$ whose length is the value of the
base-two digits of $w$. The machine reaches its completion state at some time $T \le
C(|y|+1)+2|w|$, without reaching that state earlier; it advances the input head by
$|y|$, writes $y$ on tape $d$ starting at that tape's initial head position, and leaves
the output unchanged. Tape $j$ still contains a word $w'$ of length $|w|$ on the
interval starting at its initial head position, and all other tape contents are
preserved; the head on tape $d$ advances by $|y|$, while the other work-tape head
positions are unchanged.
\end{theorem}
